A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same IMPRINT research work. All 26 pages in each version, including Appendix A.1–A.6, are readable and support comparison of text, equations, tables, and figures.

before.justification: v3 reports original classification benchmarks, component ablations, low-data experiments, neural-collapse analyses, and supplementary accuracy and runtime results.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical results in Sections 5.1–5.3 and Appendix A.

M1.justification: The IMPRINT generation, normalization, and aggregation procedures are unchanged, as are the proposed k-means configuration and the appendix's k-least-squares algorithm.

E1.justification: Both use the same MNIST, FashionMNIST, CIFAR-10, ImageNet remapping, and CombiDigits tasks, including the same four constituent digit datasets.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains Qi, Hosoda, and Janson as comparators and the least-squares oracle. Comparator membership also matches throughout the component experiments and appendix comparisons.

E3.justification: The four pretrained models, 48 model-task combinations, low-data sampling procedures, ImageNet remapping protocol, metrics, and normalization settings are unchanged.

E4.justification: Component ablations, proxy-count and sample-count sweeps, neural-collapse analyses, architectural comparisons, and supplementary least-squares analyses are retained without revision.

E5.justification: Both report the same three-seed and five-seed procedures, standard deviations, 95% confidence intervals, and Friedman and Wilcoxon–Holm significance testing.

E6.justification: Numerical results and plotted findings match throughout. For example, Table 1 retains 91.06% accuracy for Ours and 94.54% for the oracle; appendix accuracy and runtime results are also unchanged.

T1.justification: The NC1 definition in Equation (1), aggregation-equivalence reasoning, associative-memory formulation, and least-squares mathematics in Equation (A.1) are identical.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about the IMPRINT framework, multi-proxy performance, normalization, and the relationship to neural collapse.

C2.justification: Result interpretations and limitations are unchanged, including the vision-only empirical scope, remaining gap to gradient-based learning, and heuristic selection of proxy count.

D1.justification: Implementation descriptions, dataset details, regularization values, hardware and runtime disclosures, and code-access information match. The new OpenReview link supplies publication context rather than technical reproducibility information.

R1.justification: The cited works, related-work discussion, and positioning relative to prior imprinting and neural-collapse research are unchanged.

P1.justification: v4 adds a TMLR publication notice and a Reviewed on OpenReview line, and updates the arXiv version/date. Scientific prose and section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: v4 adds a running publication header and reflows introductory text across pages 1–2. Figures and tables are unchanged; rendered pages 3–26 otherwise match exactly.

improvement.justification: v4 adds publication and review metadata with limited opening-page reflow. The scientific content, supporting evidence, reproducibility information, and limitations remain identical, including the appendices, establishing no meaningful overall quality difference.
